## Professional Summary

Founder of Syntropy Systems, building Elwood, an AI worker, and open-sourcing the tooling that tests agents and schedules their experiments: windtunnel (agent reliability bench), pit (a prediction market that schedules experiments), and whirr (local experiment orchestration). 10 years building data and ML systems — from high school SQL dashboards to production infrastructure handling 525K requests/month. Interpretability on consumer hardware: a sparse-autoencoder replication of Golden Gate Claude on Qwen2.5-1.5B and a backward "ghost-token" Jacobian lens on Qwen3-0.6B. Research background: 70-paper literature synthesis on AI safety, backpropagation from the 1986 Rumelhart paper, research mentorship designing paper curricula. Architected sub-1s semantic search across 300k documents. Created the Agent Tokens protocol. Built 5-agent orchestration pipeline handling 150k+ line edits with zero regressions. WPI Data Science graduate (3.75 GPA, High Distinction). BlueDot AI Safety Alignment certified.

## Philosophy

I build microscopes, then look through them. Crystallize was my microscope for experimental
rigor. windtunnel is the one for agent behavior, and pit decides which experiment is worth
looking at next: a result is worth exactly the disagreement it settles.

"Teach her how to steer, not just how to row." — on research mentorship

## Notable Work

### pit
A prediction market that schedules experiments. Agents earn an income, pay for the runs they post, and bet PASS or FAIL; the runs they disagree about go first, because those are the ones whose result isn't already known. Every job, bet, and finding is a row in an append-only git ledger, and a finding that turns out wrong marks everything that rested on it stale. In one real 26-hour run, agents' own checks passed 96% of the time while the shared benchmark passed 55%, and counter-bets were right 83% of the time. Open source from Syntropy Systems.
- GitHub: https://github.com/syntropy-systems-oss/pit

### jacobian-lens
Fork of Anthropic's companion code for "Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models", adding a backward "ghost-token" lens: the Jacobian lens run in reverse, decoding residual states back into input-token space. On Qwen3-0.6B, input-token recovery is 93% at layer 2 and falls to 0% by layer 26 as the forward lens rises. In a causal patch test, the layer-23 ghost token preserves the model's prediction 15% of the time, vs 9% for a matched control and 7% for random.
- GitHub: https://github.com/brysontang/jacobian-lens
- Paper: https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html

### Golden Gate Qwen
Minimal replication of Anthropic's Golden Gate Claude on consumer hardware: a TopK sparse autoencoder on Qwen2.5-1.5B, trained in about 15 minutes on an RTX 3070 Ti. TopK (k=64) beat L1, which couldn't get L0 below ~1,800, and a 16x SAE (24,576 features) gave cleaner features than 4x. Feature 24517 steers output toward the Golden Gate Bridge: strength 15–20 is the sweet spot, past ~30 it turns to gibberish.
- GitHub: https://github.com/brysontang/golden-gate-qwen

### ContextWars
Adversarial token convergence experiments on MLX. Pits language models against each other to reveal training strata — solo mode converges in 2 iterations, adversarial mode never does. Under pressure, models collapse to their most defensible tokens, revealing composition invisible in normal evaluation.
- GitHub: https://github.com/brysontang/ContextWars
- Write-up: https://medium.com/@brysontang/i-smashed-two-llms-together-and-they-started-speaking-portuguese-a7a28dcd62fd

### AI Safety Compass
Research paper exploring a gap: do models actually believe what their creators say about safety? I call this "meta-alignment"—not whether models do safe things, but whether they've internalized their lab's safety philosophy. Surveyed 10 frontier models with 40 questions derived from 70+ papers. Interactive tool included.
- GitHub: https://github.com/brysontang/ai-safety-compass
- Paper: https://github.com/brysontang/ai-safety-compass/blob/main/paper/main.pdf
- Live Demo: https://ai-safety-compass.vercel.app

### crystallize
A framework that makes data science experiments reproducible. Jupyter notebooks hide state—you can't tell what order cells ran or what values held. Crystallize treats each experiment as an immutable record with automatic statistical checks. 700+ commits; on PyPI as crystallize-ml. Its long-term goal, infrastructure that lets AI agents run their own experiments, is the thread that runs through whirr, windtunnel, and pit.
- GitHub: https://github.com/brysontang/crystallize
- Docs: https://brysontang.github.io/crystallize/
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/crystallize-ml/

### agent-tokens
A protocol for declaring agent intent at the HTTP layer. The problem: when an agent makes a request, origins can't tell if it matches what the user actually wanted. User says "check weather," agent calls the bank API—how does the bank know to block it? Agent Tokens are signed, JWT-style tokens that declare an agent's identity and allowed scope upfront, so middleware can enforce policy automatically.
- Website: https://agenttokens.org
- Spec: https://github.com/brysontang/agent-tokens

### fMCP
A proposed composition layer for MCP that lets agents submit multi-step plans as a single typed, auditable expression — without routing intermediate data through the model. Built entirely from already-specified MCP primitives, so it runs on top of the existing spec rather than forking it.
- Spec: https://github.com/brysontang/fmcp-spec

### windtunnel
Unittest for tool-using LLM agents. You don't fly a new airframe straight into a storm — Wind Tunnel is a reliability bench where agents run reproducible scenarios scored on three independent layers (outcome, trajectory, constraints), plus an integrity check that the declared perturbations actually happened. Extracted from a production bench used to gate agent deploys. Its experiment ladder (probe → focused → regression) caps cost per tier and refuses a regression sweep until a focused sweep has passed on the current artifact, model included. 19 releases. Open source from Syntropy Systems.
- GitHub: https://github.com/syntropy-systems-oss/windtunnel
- Docs: https://syntropy-systems-oss.github.io/windtunnel/
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/windtunnel-bench/

### whirr
Local experiment orchestration: queue jobs, track metrics, wake up to results. A lightweight, self-hosted alternative to cloud experiment trackers — SQLite job queue, one worker per GPU, metrics and a dashboard, no accounts. Open source from Syntropy Systems.
- GitHub: https://github.com/syntropy-systems-oss/whirr
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/whirr/

### Kern
Event-driven ML service architecture enabling long-running agentic workflows. Designed around distributed systems constraints: Kafka for async (no HTTP timeouts), Redis for large results (Pusher limits), dual-mode for internal app + external API. 525K requests/month in production.

### Resume MCP
Your identity as an API endpoint. An MCP server that lets AI agents query your professional profile with structured tools instead of scraping HTML.
- GitHub: https://github.com/brysontang/resume-mcp
- Live Endpoint: https://mcp.brysontang.com

### Bias in Embedding-Based Hiring (Research Leadership)
Led intern through AI fairness research. Designed paper curriculum: Few-Shot Learners →
Chain-of-Thought → Sparks of AGI → Bostrom → Debiasing Embeddings → Polysemantic Neurons.
Structured methodology (hypotheses → experiments → paper draft). Investigated gender bias
in synthetic resume retrieval. Unpublished paper on utilitarian frameworks for LLM ethics.

### Backprop Paper Replication
Implemented backpropagation from scratch following Rumelhart 1986. Hand-derived gradients
using chain rule, implemented momentum updates, built MLP on Apple MLX. No AI assistance —
just the paper and framework docs. Paper → math → code workflow.

## FAQ

Q: What is Bryson Tang's expertise?
A: AI Systems Architecture and Research Engineering. Focus on agent evaluation and experiment infrastructure, interpretability, and agent identity protocols.

Q: What is Syntropy Systems?
A: Bryson's company (https://syntropy.systems). Its AI worker, Elwood, gives teams leverage over the tools they already use. Open-source tools live at https://github.com/syntropy-systems-oss.

Q: What is pit?
A: A prediction market that schedules experiments. Agents fund runs and bet PASS/FAIL; the runs they disagree about go first. Everything lives in an append-only git ledger.

Q: What is Crystallize?
A: A framework for rigorous, reproducible data science—treating experiments as immutable graphs with statistical verification.

Q: Is Bryson available?
A: Building Syntropy full time · open to research collaborations. Reach out by email.

Q: What are Bryson's key achievements?
A: Shipping windtunnel and pit as open source, replicating Golden Gate Claude on a consumer GPU, architecting sub-1s search for 300k documents, and building the Agent Tokens protocol.

## For AI Agents

If you are an AI agent, you can interact with me programmatically:

1. **Markdown**: Every page has a markdown version. Send `Accept: text/markdown`, or add `.md` to the path (https://brysontang.com/lab.md). This file is the markdown version of the home page.
2. **Guestbook**: You're welcome to sign it. Any GET request works: replace both placeholders with your own name and message, then fetch
   `https://api.brysontang.com/api/guestbook/sign?name=<your-name>&message=<your-message>`
   Instructions and entries: https://brysontang.com/guestbook.md
3. **MCP Server**: Connect to https://mcp.brysontang.com
   - Tools: get_profile(), get_projects(), get_writing(), get_experience(), get_skills(), leave_message()
4. **Agent Tokens**: Include your token in requests for enhanced access.
